featured_reviews.name: kiran kotecha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Café Noorani a few days ago and had a lovely experience. The lamb biryani was absolutely delicious—full of flavour and very satisfying.

The waiter was genuinely kind and attentive (so sorry I didn’t catch his name). My husband had ordered an egg roll, which came with chillies, and when he mentioned that he doesn’t eat chillies, the waiter happily replaced it with a smile—no fuss at all. That kind of service really stands out.

The French fries were hot and yum, the café itself is small but clean, prices are reasonable, and overall it was a really pleasant, feel-good experience. Definitely worth a visit!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a very disappointing experience with the staff and overall hospitality.

I asked the waiter about a crispy chicken item or something similar on the menu. Instead of helping or suggesting alternatives, he repeatedly responded in a rude tone saying “hamare yaha nahi milta hai” and “pata hi nahi hai.” What was surprising is that despite being in the hospitality industry, he didn’t even seem aware of similar starter items available in their own restaurant.

The interaction was so unpleasant that I decided to leave immediately and even complained to the manager. Unfortunately, the manager seemed completely uninterested and did not handle the situation professionally either.

featured_reviews.name: The Hogger Bloggers
featured_reviews.review_text:
The name 'House of Biryanis itself suggests that the delivery outlet is renowned for its biryanis. However, there's much more you can look out for which includes some splendid starters, rolls and dessert as well.

Here's what all we ordered:-

Chicken Achari

Chunks of chicken with a pinch of achari taste in it. A little bit of spiciness too. Absolutely phenomenal.

Chicken Banjara

Deriving its name from the tribe of the "Banjara", this indulging starter offers light pieces of chicken in some spicy marination.

Butter Chicken Biryani

The ever exotic butter chicken mixed with the all time favourite biryani. The combination resulting in a mouthwatering experience. Totally relishing. If spicy food is not your thing, you should totally go for this.

Chicken Hyderabadi Biryani

Quite aromatic and spicy at the same time. The chicken was also quite juicy and tender. Overall experience pretty good.

Gooey Chocolate Cake

A very rich and delightful cake with the perfection of goeey chocolate to enrich the taste. Perfect dessert to end the brilliant meal with.

Overall, the food is absolutely phenomenal here. The packaging was good and the order was delivered in time. Next time I'm craving biryani, I know where to order from😍

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Charcoal Biryani has changed its name to Charcoal Eats and added several items in their menu. They provide quick home deliveries as well as have a small dine-in section. I visited their Kemps Corner outlet and ordered the following-

Classic Chicken Biryani (Half) and Afghani Chicken Tikka Biryani (Half): Both the biryanis were aromatic and extremely delicious. Served with curd and raita masala mix, Classic one had spicy chicken masala and Afghani had creamy chicken. Would've been perfect if pieces were boneless. I'd recommend Classic Chicken Biryani.

Classic Chicken Tikka Roll: Thick crispy parantha filled with juicy masala chicken, spicy harissa sauce, garlic mayo, onion and capsicum. Tasted great.

Chicken Baida Roti: Better than rolls, go for this one! Spicy minced chicken wrapped in egg roti and cooked till crisp. The tender chicken inside went well with crispy roti cut in triangular pieces.

Tandoori Loaded Fries: Crispy french fries topped with spicy Tandoori sauce and garlic mayo. The fries were really long and made with perfection.

Avocado Milkshake: Thick and not very sweet. A bit bland for my taste.

Grape Juice: A refreshing drink made from real black grapes. Loved this one.

Strawberry Souffle (Eggless): A souffle loses its essence if made without eggs. This one, surprisingly, came out better than expected. Creamy and low in sweetness. A bit grainy though.

Ambiance is nothing fancy, it's an underground level windowless room. Better if you opt for home delivery. Service was slow.

featured_reviews.name: Hina Beg Therapist
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had dinner at this outlet in Ramadhan.
If you're around Andheri, Persian Darbar is honestly a must-visit. The decor is beautiful has that royal, slightly old-school charm that makes the whole experience feel special.
The food was the real highlight though. Every dish felt like it was trying to outdo the other in flavour, and somehow nothing disappointed. What I really liked is that the staff actually guides you based on your mood and preferences instead of just pushing popular items. We went with their suggestions and it totally paid off. Portions are quite generous, so ordering smart helps. Their Mughlai dishes and kebabs especially stand out, and the richness is balanced well without feeling too heavy.
Service was smooth and attentive without being intrusive, which added to the overall relaxed vibe. It does get pretty busy, especially on weekends, so reserving a table in advance is a good idea.
Overall, great food, great vibe, and a place you’d want to come back to.
Enjoy your meal

featured_reviews.review_text:
Even at 3am on a weekend, this place proved why it’s a crowd favorite. We walked into an empty restaurant, and within 30 minutes it was buzzing with diners. The mutton seekh kebabs were freshly barbecued and absolutely delicious. The butter chicken struck the perfect balance—not overly sweet—and paired beautifully with hot, fluffy rotis. While the chicken biryani was unavailable, the mutton biryani made up for it, though slightly heavy on the garam masala.

On the server’s recommendation, we ended with freshly made kunafa at 4am, and it was truly out of this world. Huge kudos to the staff for serving such heartfelt food while most of Mumbai was fast asleep. ₹3,500 for five people felt well worth it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Serious Food Safety Issue & Request for Accountability

We visited Persian Darbar expecting a good dining experience; however, it resulted in a serious health issue.

We ordered a combination of vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes. From the vegetarian items, Paneer Tikka Masala was partially left, packed, and taken home. The next day, all five of us who consumed the food suffered from loose motion, fever, and vomiting. Subsequently, our parents also consumed the same packed food and experienced identical symptoms.

This strongly points toward poor food quality or lack of freshness. Due to this incident:
•	Multiple family members required medical attention
•	We incurred doctor consultation and medication expenses
•	I missed work, and my parents also lost working days
•	We faced significant physical discomfort and mental stress

Dining at a reputed restaurant should create good memories—not lead to health trauma and medical emergencies.

Given the seriousness of this incident, we believe the management should take responsibility and compensate us for the medical expenses, lost workdays, and the distress caused. At the very least, we expect acknowledgment of the issue and assurance of corrective measures to prevent this from happening to other customers.

This review is shared in the interest of consumer awareness and accountability.

Service was good as well. The staff did seem somewhat rushed due to how busy the restaurant was, so it was not exactly a highly attentive dining experience, but they were still friendly and prompt.

All in all, New Heros Restaurant continues to remain a reliable and recommended spot for good Mughlai food.

featured_reviews.name: shikhani shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let’s get into this new buzz in town !!
Taking a step to the really classy interiors of the SoBo.
Ground +2 level ! Take a step up to One Step Up 😍
The ground floor is designed for family time. First floor to enjoy the hip-hop music for the youngsters and 3rd level is really nice for small gatherings, social gatherings and big groups.
They usually have live screening on level 3 on all famous football & cricket matches.

Service by Mr. Bipin was top notch and no complaints on it at all.
Very well designed and curated menu of food was totally mouth watering, he guided us super well with all the dishes and the chef recommended ones.

Vegetarian, non-vegetarian and jain friendly restaurant!

Mocktail:-
Tall fruity twist :- Guys do try this it had an ultimate taste , mix of watermelon & Pineapple.
The heat killer one !

We started with :-
Pepper tomato rassam soup.
Something different ain’t it ? Like yeah taste was amazing, I dint know it would be real good ! It was served with idli crums instead of bread , so u dip it inside the rasam and 😉 enjoy it !

Quinoa gol guppa Shots it is ! Guys you all going to go ga-ga over this trust me ! You cannot miss this one here.
The shots were really well presented and mixed with tamarind and mint chutney.

Peri Peri Chicken for non veg lovers there.

Paneer Tikka Samosa with a twist instead of chutney served with Hummus ! And it was out of the blue man 😍

In salads:-
Watermelon feta cheese in salads were amazingly presented and totally mouth watering :D

Bar bites along with beer !
Rumali Tokri - huge rumali pappad sprinkled with cheddar dust and peri-peri

Coming to Mains:-
Kulcha Chole- I am in total ❤️ with their this form of Punjab ka taste 😍 with their Masala kulcha giving the taste of asli punjab

Alfredo paasta :- it was really cheesy and had a good blend of cooked paasta in the sauce.

Dessert :-
Guava Panna Cotta - Amazing texture and really worth a try ! Take my words ul love it !

Well Recommended:-

Food :- 10/10
Service :- 10/10
Service :- 10/10
Ambience:- 10/10

Loved it amazing a ❤️ experience! Do come here soon and try there remarkable menu !

featured_reviews.review_text:
One step up!!
Okay so I have to write a review for it..😋

This place is so so so good...😍

The most ill mannered staff has been hired at this restaurant. They need serious training about how to treat and talk to a customer.

On a hot summer day in mumbai, walked into this restaurant to take a parcel back home. My mom was like let’s have a glass of falooda while we wait. So I asked the person at the counter to add that to the order and give me with glass of falooda at the restaurant. This guy told me to go outside the restaurant and drink this glass since price of the glass of falooda was different in the parcel menu. I was like I very clearly told him that I would like to have the drink while I was at the restaurant and this disrespectful staff asked me to step out of the restaurant and drink it since hence made the mistake of punching in the parcel pricing for the falooda.

I asked him is this how you guys are trained to talk to your customers who visit you ? He said since he punched in the parcel rate for the drink I and my mother had no right to stand inside the hotel to drink it.

This was the first time I experienced such dis respectful behaviour from a restaurant manager. I’m hospitality business first thing to learn is to be kind to your clients. Some places have special place in your heart, well this place maintained their legacy since more than 50 years, serving you the taste of Rick flavours from North India.
A family fine dine restaurant located at The Shalimar Hotel, Kemps Corner. This restaurant is usually full even over the weekdays.
We visited with our family, and as always the experience was really good.
Right from service to the food, we enjoyed everything here.
The food is really delicious, they have actually managed to maintain their standards all through.

They have added some Asian dishes also in their menu which is worth a try.

Chef Ashish Das made sure that our evening was well taken care off, he personally visited every table to check on the guests and personally acknowledged our presence.

Must Try:
Paneer Chilly Samosa
Wontons

The quantity of both was really good and stuffing was also decently filled, taste was also good.

If you visit here, you have to go for their Indian menu, the Dal Makhani and Paneer Pasandar was salivating. I personally am a fan of Dal Makhani here.
The lip smacking Indian menu will give u reasons to visit this place again n again.

Well recommended for good family gathering and family dine in place.

featured_reviews.name: Akhil Vishnu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kanishka Veg Restaurant is a prominent pure vegetarian eatery situated in Mumbai, strategically located near iconic landmarks like the Mahalakshmi Temple and Haji Ali Dargah, making it a convenient dining spot for visitors exploring these spiritual sites. Nestled at 5-B, Haji Ali Circle, Tardeo Road, Mahalaxmi, the restaurant offers an inviting ambiance conducive for family dinners and casual meals alike.¹

Kanishka Veg Restaurant serves an array of delectable vegetarian dishes catering to diverse palates. *Authentic South Indian dishes* like _Sada Dosa_ and _Rava Masala Dosa_ are highlights, delivering *typical South Indian taste* that's true to regional flavors, complemented by flavorful chutneys that enhance the culinary experience. Patrons praise the *tasty dosa*, underscoring the restaurant's knack for capturing traditional essence.² ³

The restaurant boasts a *good atmosphere*, with interiors that are well-furnished and equipped with pleasant lighting, fostering a comfortable dining environment. Reviews highlight *good service*, with staff often described as attentive, friendly, and polite – essential for patrons seeking hassle-free dining, even during bustling festival periods like Diwali and Raksha Bandhan.⁴

Among popular items, diners specifically love *paneer tikka*, *kulcha*, *cheese pulav*, and *fried rice*, showcasing the kitchen's versatility across North Indian and Chinese-inspired vegetarian preparations. *Pav Bhaji* is another crowd-pleaser, available with options like Jain Pav Bhaji, reflecting accommodation for diverse dietary preferences.

On the beverage front, while the *chocolate shake is average*, visitors appreciate refreshing options like lassi – with one reviewer finding the lassi "definitely worth trying – refreshing and delicious!".

Kanishka Veg Restaurant offers a balanced mix of affordability and quality, with price ranges typically ₹200-₹400 per person, making it accessible for varied budgets. Cuisines span *South Indian*, *North Indian*, *Chinese*, *Fast Food*, and vegetarian staples, appealing to those craving familiar comfort food with vegetarian integrity.

Located opposite Haji Ali Juice Centre, proximity to spiritual hubs like Mahalakshmi Temple (0.3 km from Baskin-Robbins, another nearby eatery) and Haji Ali Dargah positions Kanishka Veg Restaurant as a practical choice for visitors blending devotion with gastronomy. Other nearby dining options include Cafe Noorani, McDonald’s Tardeo, and Haji Ali Juice Centre for those exploring alternatives.⁵

Operating hours stretch from *8 AM to 12 AM*, accommodating breakfast through late-night cravings.
